I still remembered my Intro to Bayesian Analysis course, and that period was a fond memory. It was spring and right outside the dorm, there are the cherry trees. A whole forest of them. They were part of this landscaping project started by the generosity of an alumni, and have now became a university's staple. The student newspaper would track the blossom dates meticulously and everyone would just come to this part of the campus to look at the trees. They were all waiting, and I was too. And one day, the blossoms had started. It was a full bloom. They were pink and vibrant. Even smelled great too. Looking at them from the window gave me a sense of longing - of how nice it must be to share that patch under the tree with another person. But there isn't anyone at the time and the only person who would was too far.

## Introduction

Here's a simple question: "What is the chance that it will rain tomorrow?"

You might think that this is an easy question to answer. Open your weather app and there it is: 55%.

But what does that 55% mean? To understand that we need a coin.

Think about how we usually make sense of probability. Suppose we want to know what is the probability of flipping a head.
